original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Can scripts/shared_point_circuit.py:SharedPointCircuit.verify emit the same circuit_sha256 digest lines (and the same support/topology assertion checks) without per-node json.dumps, so full-size shared-point and bit-compression verify receipts stay fieldwise identical?
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for one measured replay bottleneck with before/after wall time and retained checks. Expertise override selected verifier-engineering after open tooling PR #1984 left SharedPointCircuit.verify / ExclusionCircuit.verify digests as an explicit next question. Profiling named SharedPointCircuit.verify's per-node json.dumps stream (about half of h=46 verify time) as the bottleneck; ExclusionCircuit.verify's single json.dumps is not hot.
bottleneck_link: Side result on review throughput: shared-point verify and bit-compression certificates call SharedPointCircuit.verify. A faster identical digest does not change kappa or the binding complex supplier.
stop_rule: Ship an equivalence-preserving SharedPointCircuit.verify digest change with frozen baseline, identical receipts on the historical h=46 circuit, registered replay and a measured before/after median. Do not reopen the mathematical screens, rewrite ExclusionCircuit support enumeration, or run the selected cold frontier replay.
evidence: PASS_SHARED_POINT_DIGEST via research/shared-point-digest/verify.py (also under -O); PASS_IDENTICAL_SHARED_POINT_DIGEST_RECEIPTS via benchmark.py; bit-compression certificate does not pin scripts/shared_point_circuit.py in source_sha256.
author: Wentao Li
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance for orientation, overlap search, profiling, implementation, packaging, benchmarking and writing. Not independent human peer review.

open_questions.question: Should research/bit-compression-provenance refresh its live scripts/shared_point_circuit.py SHA-256 pin after this equivalence-preserving digest rewrite?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That provenance package binds working-tree bytes of shared_point_circuit.py; leaving the old pin keeps this tooling PR focused, but a later full provenance replay on main would see a hash mismatch until refreshed.
open_questions.first_step: Open a dedicated provenance follow-up that only rewrites the shared_point_circuit.py entry in SOURCES.json after confirming circuit_sha256 identity.
open_questions.blocked_by: Pin repair is outside this tooling change.

open_questions.question: Is ExclusionCircuit.verify's leave-two-out expected-support genexpr worth a separate identical-receipt rewrite?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Profiling shows that single json.dumps is negligible there; the hot path is the per-output support sum genexpr, a different object from digest formatting.
open_questions.first_step: Profile ExclusionCircuit(45).verify alone and prototype a closed-form support mask if one matches the historical expected bits.
open_questions.blocked_by: Out of this session's stop rule; SharedPointCircuit.verify digests were the measured bottleneck.
